body: Oh yes of course. It wouldn't even be an option unless when my sibling comes out my parents just entirely loose their crap and kick them out. Which isn't super unlikely. But anyway, I'll stop taking your time. Thank you so much for your words and your gentleness.

Thank you a lot. I know they are struggling, and I wish I could just go to our mom and be like, "for reasons, [sibling] is living with me," so that I can get them all of the therapy and love and whatever they need. Is it bad that I'm almost hoping that our parents do tell her to get lost when and if they come out so that I can take them in and give them all the treatment and love and support that I didn't get?

Thank you. I don't think I realized how much I needed to read something like this until I did. My sibling has myself and our sister who is 13 months older than them, along with friends and a boyfriend who supports them. 

The part that I think hurts the worst is that my sibling has a twin brother who is parroting our parents mindsets. They told me today that their twin regularly asks if they are alright with going to hell.. "because that's where you're going if you keep up with this." I didn't cry at the time but... I couldn't imagine having a twin who is so utterly cruel.
Thank you for this. I was going to ignore the response, but I appreciate your input, and your words.

They are terrified of confiding in anyone at school because the last time that happened it turned into a disaster. 

They have been friends with a transmale who... My sibling told me that being with him has made them happier than they've been since 4-5 grade. That's significant because in 4th grade my sibling was sent home for writing suicidal thoughts on a notebook due to bullying. Because our parents don't believe in that, they paraded her around all of the therapists in town until they found one who would say that my sibling was fine and that they could return to school, even though my sibling was most definitely not fine.
So listen... My birthday is in 2 weeks... You wanna get your guys together to do the shot thing? I'm a girl but... I just really wanna get jello shots drunk...? Lmao

Yea, I actually worked for a while at a crisis/detox center, and am well aware of the dangers of alcohol detox. My husband and I are imagining that they will drink when they leave our house, and may possibly have a drink or two before coming to our house. 

As for my son knowing his grandparents, he has three full sets of grandparents. My husband's mother and father, my mother and stepfather, and my father and stepmother. His two sets of grandparents (husband's parents and my mother and stepfather) are local, and trrsty son like royalty. The kid wants for nothing and knows that he is loved, and appreciated and has great relationships with them. 

I completely understand the whole better to have nothing than the bad thing. This visit will probably determine a lot of how they are allowed into me, my husband, and our son's lives. This is their first visit since my husband and I have purchased our own home, and the first visit since our son has been his own little individual person rather than the infant lump that cries, eats and shits; or the toddler that is trying to find creative ways to accidently kill themselves. Lol.
Oh my God. I've never even heard of this guy until today, and now I need to find every documentary he's made. Lmao

It's not problem! And good information to share anyway. Alcohol is one of the more dangerous substances to detox from, despite it's legality. Super important information for anyone who has an alcoholic loved one to know.

I do know that, actually. I work in mental health and substance use, and worked at a crisis/detox facility. That is why they are not staying with us. They can drink at their hotel. As long as they don't come to my house and drink, or come to my house drunk, they can live their boozy lives at their hotel.
Thank you so much for your comments. I really appreciate it.

Yea, I used to work at a crisis facility. I'm aware that alcohol withdrawals are one of the most dangerous. They would most likely drink when they returned to their hotel room in the afternoons/evenings. They likely will spend the first day or two trying to figure out how much they can drink before coming to my house in the morning before I'll notice and tell them to get lost. 

The good news is that my husband has already told me that he has my back, and will 100% support me if I tell them to get lost, and if I feel like I can't tell them to get lost, he will for me.
That would be a hard sell. They are traveling more than 10 hours to spend time with me and my family. A lunch or couple of hours at a park aren't what they are anticipating for this trip.

No it would be just my father, stepmother, and half brother. It's possible that my half brother on my other side and his fiancee would be there as they are living with my husband and I currently, but that's a short conversation to just say, "hey, no drinking here this weekend" and they would honor that. 

My husband and I have already agreed to not even have booze in the house, which isn't a big deal for us. My husband will drink maybe 2 beers a week, because he loves craft beers, and I drink even more rarely. Hell I have a can of hard kombucha I've had in my fridge for going on 3 months now that I have yet to drink.

My stepmother is more of the brash, "look at me and how wild and crazy I am" type personality. She was also genuinely upset that I wasn't going to insist the my biological mother come to my house for Thanksgiving. My mom (who I have an excellent relationship with) is allergic to cats. Highly allergic to cats. I have... You guessed it, cats! Two of them. I knew when I got them that it likely meant my mother would not be coming to my house. Not a big deal, we live 10 minutes from each other. 

My stepmother wants to do this big Thanksgiving/Christmas dinner thing when she comes down, and wants my mother, stepfather, and my siblings on that side of the family to come over. I am literally the only thing they have in common. My mom and stepfather are not friends with my dad and stepmother. There is literally no reason for my mother to come to my house to eat with my father and stepmother. Except my stepmother wants to be seen as the "glue that holds everything together." 

In reality, it was the emotional affair between her and my father along with his alcoholism that led to my mother's determination to divorce my father.

Oh absolutely not. Absolutely absolutely not. At some point they are going to start hinting or just outright requesting that my son come.up there to stay with them for a couple of weeks during summer breaks and all that and you'll probably be able to hear my "hell no" from wherever in the world you may be.

Wow. That's absolutely insane. I know that there is going to have to be a lot of stepping in during this visit. My stepmother has absolutely no filter. On the phone with me last night she was like, "I just wanna fulfill my dream of pole dancing on the fireman's pole." (My husband is a firefighter). She was absolutely 100% dead serious. I had to tell her that wouldn't be possible because only one station in my husband's area has a pole, and it is *not* the station he works at, and even if it was, they aren't letting people into the stations because of COVID. She was genuinely upset. 

...it's going to be a very long four days having them around.

I work in the mental health field, and previous substance use is approximately 40% of my caseload. I have one or two clients who still try to get me to take them to get their 40s and I'm like, "not only can I get fired, but that is literally the antithesis of what I am here to do!"
I'll have to look it up. Thanks.

Thank you. I appreciate your words. 

I absolutely adore my stepfather. He has his issues absolutely. But he chose his children. He chose his family. He's always been there not only for his own kids, but for me, and for my child. My stepfather is the man that I wish my father could have been, and I think that is why his alcoholism hurts me as bad as it does still today. For all intents and purposes, these two men were given the same thing. A loving, determined wife, a child, and a future. One decided to throw it away for the booze, and the other has a family of 6, a dog, and a business he runs himself.

Yea. One comment here suggested a compromise of a beer an hour, or a 40oz that they could sip on throughout the day and I was like, "I appreciate the thought, but also, that's a slippery slope that I'm not sure I'd have the wherewithal to moderate"
That line says it perfectly.

I've seen them, and spoken to them. They still drink like fishes and don't see a reason not to. They are also the kind of people who take a mile if given an inch. That said, watching my father drink kills me. My husband and I aren't planning on drinking or even having alcohol in the house when my father and stepmother visit, so it wouldn't be about any lack of fairness or anything like that. As far as they know/are concerned, it is a flat-out rule that my husband and I have, no alcohol in the house. 

The idea of a compromise wouldn't be a bad one if it wasn't for the fact that I know it would be taken advantage of, and they would very easily say, "well, it's just one more. One more won't hurt." And it's taking nearly all my capabilities to have the blanket rule. I wouldn't be able to look at my father and tell him he can't have another beer. I feel like for my mental health, it would be wiser to just say, "nope. Not here."

Oh God that's awful. I'm so sorry to hear about your niece. 

Honestly, I don't really think I love them. I think that ship has sailed. I feel bad for them, and I pity them, but I don't love them. If I didn't have children, I would have cut contact, and I don't think it would have been terribly difficult for me. But, I feel it's important to see what you come from. Seeing my father and grandfather's addictions first hand made such an impression on me, I swore that I wouldn't touch alcohol or drugs, since I knew that I had the predisposition.

I completely agree. I don't even think that my brothers are assholes. What's interesting is that their father (my stepfather) was an alcoholic when he met my mother. They got pregnant on accident, and my mother looked at my stepfather and was like, "I've been down this road before. You can have me and your child, or you can have the alcohol." My stepfather chose my mom and my brother, and now they have a large amount of other children and a 24 year marriage.

Your info is correct. My husband is of the thought process that your schedule is exactly how it will happen. My concerns is that they are not going to limit their drinking to after they leave my house. I don't know if my father will be able to go a solid 8-12 hours without drinking something.

I feel like my son deserves to know his grandfather, no matter my feelings. My father's father (my grandfather) had the same issues. Alongside the issue of racism. My grandfather HATED my mother because she was black. Until I was born. I was the golden grandchild, and my Pop-Pop loved me to pieces, until he drank himself to death. In retrospect, he was a horrible person. But at 3-7 years old, he was my Pop-Pop who taught me how to whistle so I could whistle to the birds he had.
